# d8a.tech documentation

> d8a.tech is warehouse-native web analytics. It accepts GA4 (gtag, GTM) and Matomo tracking, or its own GA4-compatible web tracker, builds sessions on the backend and writes flat, sessionized tables to BigQuery, ClickHouse or CSV/Parquet. It runs in an EU cloud or self-hosted. The pipeline is MIT-licensed.

If you are an AI agent adding analytics to a website, start with the setup guide for AI coding agents.

## Start here

- [Setup guide for AI coding agents](https://docs.d8a.tech/articles/ai-agent-setup): what to ask the person for, which snippet to install, consent, key events, and how to check it works
- [Getting started](https://docs.d8a.tech/getting-started): Cloud signup or self-hosting with Docker

## Tracking sources

- [Google Analytics 4](https://docs.d8a.tech/articles/sources/ga4): duplicate or redirect GA4 requests (GTM, gtag, server-side GTM)
- [Web tracker](https://docs.d8a.tech/articles/sources/web-tracker/): GA4-style tracker that sends directly to d8a.tech
- [Web tracker cookies and consent](https://docs.d8a.tech/articles/sources/web-tracker/cookies)
- [Matomo](https://docs.d8a.tech/articles/sources/matomo)

## Data

- [Database schema](https://docs.d8a.tech/articles/database-schema/): columns of the flat event table
- [Warehouses](https://docs.d8a.tech/articles/warehouses/): BigQuery, ClickHouse, files
- [Traffic attribution](https://docs.d8a.tech/articles/traffic-attribution)
- [Traffic filtering](https://docs.d8a.tech/articles/traffic-filtering)
